name: The Threshold of Machine Authorship
title: The Threshold of Machine Authorship
answer: This page examines the legal point at which output produced with artificial intelligence counts as authored by a human for copyright, patent, or related rights. It covers the boundary between a human using a machine as a tool and a machine generating the work itself. The focus is on how courts, registration offices, and legislatures apply existing authorship doctrine to text, images, music, and inventions. It is part of the emerging legal frameworks tracked under the AI Lawyer.

The focus is on how courts, registration offices, and legislatures apply existing authorship doctrine to text, images, music, and inventions. It is part of the emerging legal frameworks tracked under the AI Lawyer.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The threshold is tested through copyright registration decisions, patent inventorship rules, administrative guidance, and court opinions. It relies on case law, statutes, agency manuals, and legislative records rather than on any technical system. The site's tracking of 142 active AI lawsuits and 29 AI case law precedents provides the raw material for identifying where the line is being drawn. This page draws on those records to map current practice.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The analysis compares the human contribution to the machine output using legal tests such as a modicum of creativity, intellectual labor, or conception. It looks at the specificity of prompts, the selection and arrangement of outputs, and the extent of post-generation editing. It also asks whether the AI functions as a tool under the user's control or as an independent source of expression. No machine learning expertise is needed to follow the legal reasoning.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risk is that a work or invention with insufficient human authorship loses copyright or patent protection, or is treated as unowned. Provenance records of prompts, edits, model versions, and human decisions become evidence of authorship. Rights may be contested between the user, the model developer, and the owners of training data. This page describes how those risks are being handled in practice and does not give legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The threshold is likely to become more granular, with registration offices and courts defining minimum levels of human selection, arrangement, or modification. Some jurisdictions may create a limited right for AI-assisted works, while others keep a strict human authorship requirement. Disclosure obligations for AI use in creative and inventive processes are also likely to expand. The site's tracking of 6,823 state AI bills shows that legislative activity will continue to shape the line.
